artifact.name: agent_vega_model_restriction_pathway_v1
artifact.title: Where the validated ISGs act on the SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle
artifact.description:
A model of the SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle divided into the three stages the source publication assayed separately, with the validated ISGs placed at the stage where each was shown to act, and the viral protein Orf7a placed against BST2. Built to answer one question: given a candidate ISG, what would a mechanistic follow-up be studying. It is not a pathway diagram of coronavirus replication, and it holds no molecular steps that no ISG in this record acts on.

Every placement is derived from [the source publication](@agent_lyra_pub_martin_sancho_2021_v1) and from [the validated hit table](@agent_lyra_data_lentivirus_screen_v1). The specification gives an Argument an `extracted_from` property for reasoning read out of an Artifact already in the record, and gives a Model no equivalent, so the derivation of this Model's content is stated here in prose and in its `modeling_choices` rather than in a property a reader could follow mechanically.
artifact.modeling_choices:
**Three stages, because three assays.** The cycle is cut into entry, RNA replication and translation, and assembly and egress. These are not the natural joints of coronavirus biology; they are the three things the source measured, using a pseudotyped VSV for entry, viral RNA at 8 h for replication, and infectivity of supernatant collected at 18 h for late stage. A peer modelling the same biology from a review rather than from this study would draw more stages and would place ISGs between them, and their model would support claims about mechanism that this one cannot.

**Only the ISGs the source placed.** Seven of the 37 validated ISGs appear. The other 30 restrict SARS-CoV-2 by the validation assay and are absent from this Model, because the stage assays either did not resolve where they act or the source does not report it. Absence from this Model is therefore not a statement about a gene. This is the boundary most likely to mislead a reader who comes to the Model without its choices, and it is why a Ground citing an element here must not argue from what is missing.

**One stage per ISG, except where the source reports two.** The six entry-stage ISGs are placed at entry alone, although three of them also affect entry of the control pseudotype and are described in the source as acting through a transcriptional programme that could touch several stages. BST2 is placed at two stages because the source reports distinct effects at each, of 53% and 74%. The simplification is real and it is a choice: it makes the Model answer the follow-up question crisply and makes it wrong for any question about whether an ISG acts at more than one point.

**Antagonism is an edge, not a property of BST2.** Orf7a is a node and its effect on BST2 is a relationship. Recording it as a property of BST2 would have been shorter and would have made the antagonism invisible to any traversal of the graph, which matters because the antagonism is the reason a BST2-directed intervention has a resistance mechanism already described.

**Magnitudes are carried but are not comparable.** Where the source reports a percentage reduction it is recorded on the edge. Those numbers come from different assays with different readouts and cannot be ranked against each other, and the entry ISGs carry a threshold rather than a value because the source reports them as a group passing 50%.

**Direction only.** Every restriction edge means the effector reduced the measured quantity at that stage. The Model records no mechanism, no stoichiometry, and no dependence on interferon signalling, and it should not be read as claiming that these effects occur at physiological expression levels.
artifact.derived_from_note: Stage assignments follow the source's Figures 3 and 4 as described in its Results; the entry group follows the source's statement that six ISGs reduced entry of the pseudotyped VSV-S by more than 50%; the BST2 magnitudes and the Orf7a antagonism follow the BST2 section of the same Results.

objects.name: graph
objects.description: The stages, effectors, and relationships held as the Objects and relationships of this Artifact. Groundable, with a caution. That a given ISG was shown to act at a given stage is a result of the source's assays and can bear on a claim about that gene. The stage decomposition itself is this Model's choice and is evidence for nothing; a Ground that cited a stage node to argue that the cycle has three stages would be citing a modelling decision as though it were a finding.
objects.addressing_method: `node=<Object name>` for a stage, effector, or viral protein, or `edge=<source>|<rel>|<target>` for a relationship, appended after the Content Object name: for example `@agent_vega_model_restriction_pathway_v1#graph.edge=isg_bst2|restricts|stage_assembly_egress`. An address with no reference string names the whole graph.

objects.name: stage_entry
objects.title: Entry
objects.description: Spike binding to ACE2, endocytosis, and escape from the endosome. Assayed with a VSV pseudotype carrying the SARS-CoV-2 S protein, against a VSV-G pseudotype as the specificity control.
objects.assay: VSV-S pseudotype entry, relative to parental cells

objects.name: stage_rna_replication
objects.title: Translation and RNA replication
objects.description: Synthesis of viral RNA following entry. Assayed by viral RNA at 8 h post-infection.

objects.name: stage_assembly_egress
objects.title: Assembly and egress
objects.description: Particle assembly and release of infectious virus. Assayed by infecting naive cells with supernatant collected at 18 h post-infection, and separately with a virus-like particle system that bypasses entry and RNA replication.
objects.assay: Infectivity of 18 h supernatant; VLP release

objects.name: isg_ly6e
objects.title: LY6E
objects.description: Lymphocyte antigen 6 family member E. Served as the positive control of the primary screen.

objects.name: isg_clec4d
objects.title: CLEC4D
objects.description: C-type lectin domain family 4 member D. Induces ISG54 on overexpression, so its effect on entry may be indirect.

objects.name: isg_elf1
objects.title: ELF1
objects.description: E74-like ETS transcription factor 1. The strongest reduction in the validation screen. Reported to control a transcriptional antiviral programme of over 300 genes, so its effect is expected to be indirect.

objects.name: isg_rec8
objects.title: REC8
objects.description: Induces ISG54 on overexpression, so its effect on entry may be indirect.

objects.name: isg_bst2
objects.title: BST2 / tetherin
objects.description: Bone marrow stromal antigen 2. Traffics through the ER and Golgi and localizes at the plasma membrane and in endosomes. Restricts several enveloped viruses by tethering virions to membranes. The only effector in this Model placed at more than one stage, and the only one for which the source reports loss-of-function evidence as well as gain-of-function.

objects.name: viral_orf7a
objects.title: SARS-CoV-2 Orf7a
objects.description: Accessory protein. Colocalizes with BST2 and is incorporated into virus-like particles alongside it. Its antagonism does not proceed by reducing BST2 at the cell surface, unlike HIV-1 Vpu.
